hook.line: Everyone in the café has a version of what would have happened. If Rosa had posted one of those letters, would Joaquín have come back? To play that game you need one frame.
hook.es: Si hubiera sabido, habría venido antes.
hook.en: If I had known, I would have come sooner.

examples.es: Si hubiera sabido, habría venido antes.
examples.en: If I had known, I would have come sooner.

examples.es: Si Rosa hubiera mandado las cartas, Joaquín habría vuelto.
examples.en: If Rosa had sent the letters, Joaquín would have come back.

examples.es: Si no hubiéramos firmado, hoy estaríamos tranquilos.
examples.en: If we hadn't signed, we'd be fine today.

examples.es: Si hubiéramos salido más temprano, no habríamos perdido el bus.
examples.en: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the bus.

examples.es: Si hubiera sabido, hubiera venido antes.
examples.en: If I had known, I would have come sooner.

rule:
To imagine a past that didn't happen, put *hubiera* plus a participle after *si*, and *habría* plus a participle in the other half:

*Si hubiera sabido* (if I had known), *habría venido* (I would have come).

The two halves can swap places: *Habría venido si hubiera sabido.* The *si* half never takes *habría*: English "if I would have known" is the trap.

If the result is about now, use the plain *-ría* ending: *Si no hubiéramos firmado, hoy estaríamos tranquilos.* In everyday Latin American speech you will also hear *hubiera* in both halves: *Si hubiera sabido, hubiera venido.* It is common and fine.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the third conditional, or the past unreal conditional (*condicional irreal de pasado*): *si* + pluperfect subjunctive, conditional perfect. With a result in the present it is called mixed.

readAndPick.es: Si hubiera sabido, habría venido antes.
options: If I know, I'll come sooner.
If I knew, I would come sooner.
If I had known, I would have come sooner.

readAndPick.es: Si no hubiéramos firmado, hoy estaríamos tranquilos.
options: If we hadn't signed, we'd be fine today.
If we don't sign, we'll be fine today.

options: Rosa sent the letters, so Joaquín came back.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right form and type the whole sentence: *Si ___ sabido, habría venido.* (*hubiera* or *habría*)
Pick the right form and type the whole sentence: *Si Vale hubiera llamado, la ___ ayudado.* (*habría* or *hubiera*)
yourTurn.answer: Si Vale hubiera llamado, la habría ayudado.
accept: Si Vale hubiera llamado, la hubiera ayudado.
yourTurn.why: The result half is the one with *habría*: what would have happened.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If I had known, I would have come sooner.
yourTurn.answer: Si hubiera sabido, habría venido antes.
accept: Si hubiera sabido, hubiera venido antes.
Habría venido antes si hubiera sabido.
yourTurn.why: *Hubiera* plus participle after *si*, *habría* plus participle for the result.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If it had rained, we wouldn't have gone.
yourTurn.answer: Si hubiera llovido, no habríamos ido.
accept: Si hubiera llovido, no hubiéramos ido.
No habríamos ido si hubiera llovido.
yourTurn.why: *No* goes right before *habríamos*, and *ido* is the participle of *ir*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If Tomás had taken the job in Toronto, he wouldn't be here today.
yourTurn.answer: Si Tomás hubiera aceptado el trabajo en Toronto, no estaría aquí hoy.
accept: Si Tomás hubiera aceptado el trabajo en Toronto, hoy no estaría aquí.
Tomás no estaría aquí hoy si hubiera aceptado el trabajo en Toronto.
yourTurn.why: The result is about today, so it is plain *estaría*, not *habría estado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *we*: *Si hubiera sabido, habría venido.*
Make it negative in the *si* half: *Si hubiera firmado, hoy estaría tranquilo.*
yourTurn.answer: Si no hubiera firmado, hoy estaría tranquilo.
accept: Hoy estaría tranquilo si no hubiera firmado.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If Vale had called, I would have helped her.
yourTurn.answer: Si Vale hubiera llamado, la habría ayudado.
accept: Si Vale hubiera llamado, la hubiera ayudado.
La habría ayudado si Vale hubiera llamado.
yourTurn.why: *La* (her) goes before *habría*, and *llamado* is the participle.

pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "if I would have known", but Spanish keeps *habría* for the result and uses *hubiera* after *si*.
*Supiera* imagines now; for something that didn't happen in the past you need *hubiera sabido*.

pitfalls.right: Si hubiera sabido, habría venido antes.
pitfalls.why: The result half needs *habría* plus the participle: it is what would have happened.

pitfalls.wrong: Si hubiera tenido plata, viajaría ayer.
pitfalls.right: Si hubiera tenido plata, habría viajado ayer.
pitfalls.why: A result that belongs to the past is *habría viajado*; plain *viajaría* only fits a result about now.

personal: Think of one small choice you made last year. Write what would have happened otherwise, starting *Si no hubiera…*.
